summary: This module defines a Dagger object that runs Python code quality tools (linting, formatting, type-checking) in isolated containers. Each method spins up a fresh Python container, installs a tool, mounts your source and config directories, and runs the tool—returning its output. The run_all method executes all four tools concurrently using async task groups instead of waiting for each one to finish sequentially.

explanations.4: Annotated is a typing feature that lets you attach extra metadata (like documentation and default paths) to a type definition without changing what the type actually is.
explanations.13: Annotated wraps the Directory type with three pieces of metadata: Doc explains what this field does, DefaultPath tells the system to look in 'src' by default if not explicitly provided, and Directory is the actual type.
explanations.27: The async keyword means this function can be paused and resumed, which is necessary because we're waiting for container operations to complete without blocking other code.
explanations.31: The await keyword pauses this function until the container chain finishes executing and returns a result; the whole .from_(...).with_exec(...) chain is building up a container operation that gets executed when awaited.
explanations.38: The --rcfile argument tells pylint where to find its configuration file; we're pointing it to the config directory we mounted into the container.
explanations.63: This creates a persistent cache volume named 'python_mypy' that survives between container runs, so mypy doesn't have to recompute type information from scratch every time.
explanations.74: The f-string (the f prefix) means we're interpolating the variable mypy_cache path directly into the command string.
explanations.98: anyio.create_task_group() sets up a context where multiple async functions can run at the same time; it waits for all of them to finish before moving on.
explanations.99: tg.start_soon schedules a task to run concurrently without waiting for it to finish immediately—all four start_soon calls queue up, then the task group runs them all in parallel.
